root_cause.text: The verify_dfa() function conditionally validates DEFAULT_TABLE bounds only when the MATCH_FLAG_DIFF_ENCODE flag is not set, allowing out-of-bounds DEFAULT_TABLE entries to pass validation when differential encoding is used, which are then dereferenced as array indices during the verification loop.
root_cause.evidence: The patch removes the `!(BASE_TABLE(dfa)[i] & MATCH_FLAG_DIFF_ENCODE) &&` condition from the bounds check, making the validation unconditional. The CVE description explicitly states: "When the verification loop traverses the differential encoding chain, it reads k = DEFAULT_TABLE[j] and uses k as an array index without validation. A malformed DFA with DEFAULT_TABLE[j] >= state_count, therefore, causes both out-of-bounds reads and writes." The original code at line 163-164 only checked `(DEFAULT_TABLE(dfa)[i] >= state_count)` when the differential encoding flag was NOT set, creating a validation gap for differentially-encoded states that could contain invalid indices.

In the new verify_dfa() function (lines 199-227), the DEFAULT_TABLE bounds check at lines 206-207 only validates when MATCH_FLAG_DIFF_ENCODE is NOT set: `if (!(BASE_TABLE(dfa)[i] & MATCH_FLAG_DIFF_ENCODE) && (DEFAULT_TABLE(dfa)[i] >= state_count))`.
